$comment: The Contributor Community (/contributing/; /roles/, /pin/ and /contributors/ redirect here). Unlisted (noindex, not linked from the program page) until the board approves the levels. The one idea: The Labs is built by the people who learn here. Learning by doing, applied to The Labs itself: anyone can contribute (make something, take a role, teach what you know, or back it as a Supporting Member; roles open in order, and Poderator comes after a Build Cycle), and each level means you've worked hands-on in more of its workstreams, major and minor. The page is three chapters, and each cover's promise is paid off by the sections right under it: Start anywhere (the ways in), Go as far as you like (the levels), Yours for good (how the pin is given, active or emeritus, what won't change). The pin recognizes new permissions and responsibilities over the playbooks, tools, program kits and platform, in your own region first (regional pins are brass, national silver; the ladder repeats upstream); it's yours forever, but the say that comes with it needs an active seat, which has to be kept up. The pins are the symbol: one section walks the levels, by scroll or by picking one, with a pin you can drag (live 3D on desktop). Summarises design/research/recognition-system.md. [PLACEHOLDER] marks what's still open. The covers reuse the program page's macro shots of the pin (src/components/JoinCover.astro): chapters[].shot picks the shot (join.json mission[n]); title is this page's tagline.
title: Contributor Community
description: The Labs is built by the people who learn here. Start anywhere, go as far as you like, and what you earn is yours for good.
draft: A working draft. The board hasn't approved the levels or the workstreams yet, and the pins are still being made.

title: Contributor
Community
hero.lede: The Labs is built by the people who learn here. That's the whole idea. Here's how you become one of them.
hero.status: The first pins go to our two steering committees
hero.pinAlt: The Contributing Member pin, turning to follow your pointer

chapters.title: Go as far as you like.

why.title: A community you can actually show up to.

items.label: In person
items.title: Close to home.
items.body: People from your own neighborhood, face to face. Not just a chat window.

items.label: Side by side
items.title: Beginners and experts, together.
items.body: Learn from people who've done it. Then teach what you know.

items.label: Hands-on
items.title: Learning is the point.
items.body: Every job here teaches you something. And with AI tools, you'll end up building more than you thought you could.

items.label: Local
items.title: Real problems, real neighbors.
items.body: What you make helps someone you might pass on the street.

start.title: There's no front door. Come in wherever you like.
start.lede: Somebody fixes a typo in the guide. Somebody else runs a whole room. It all counts, and none of it gets forgotten.

items.label: If you make things
items.title: Make something better.
items.body: See something that could be better? Change it. A guide, a flyer, a talk, a bit of code. We'll credit you by name.

items.label: If you want a job to do
items.title: Take a role.
items.body: Ambassador, Upskiller and Mentor are open now. Poderator comes after you've been through a Build Cycle yourself. Every role has its own training, and soon its own page.

items.label: If you've got something to teach
items.title: Teach what you know.
items.body: Everyone does. Mentor a pod, look over work you know well, and help newer people find their feet. Your time counts here, and we'll make sure people know it.

items.label: If you'd rather back it than build it
items.title: Become a Supporting Member.
items.body: Chip in a little each year, wear the button that says you back The Labs, and come to everything. You can always start here.

start.note: Whichever door you take, the pin works the same way. When The Labs runs on something you gave, the people who saw it happen put your name forward. Dues don't count toward it. Only the work does.

rings.title: Four levels. Each one puts more of The Labs in your hands.
rings.lede: It isn't a ladder you have to climb. Plenty of people find the job they love and stay there for years. But if you want to see how the whole thing fits together, this is how you get there.

steps.line: Something you gave is now part of how The Labs runs.
steps.how: Your work, your time, or your know-how made a real difference, and your Lab wrote down what it was.
steps.trusted: Vouching for the next person who's ready.

steps.line: You've done it, so you can check it.
steps.how: You've worked hands-on in two major workstreams, and two people who already wear the pin have vouched for you.
steps.trusted: Checking work in the areas you know, and helping newer people get there.

steps.line: You've seen every part of The Labs up close.
steps.how: You've worked hands-on in every major workstream, and a few of the smaller ones.
steps.trusted: Saying yes to changes in your Lab's playbooks, and mentoring Reviewers.

steps.line: You know how it all fits together.
steps.how: You've been hands-on across the board. The other Maintainers put your name forward, and the board says yes.
steps.trusted: Deciding where a workstream goes next. The board keeps the final say.

rings.names: Workstreams and level names are still drafts. Major workstreams (draft): Build Cycle, Learning Pathways, Community & Outreach, Platform (OLOS), Operations & Governance. Smaller ones include events, communications and research. [PLACEHOLDER]

picker.stageLabel: The {rank} pin. Drag, or use the arrow keys, to turn it.

given.title: It starts with the work. It ends with a handshake.

steps.title: Do the work.
steps.body: Give your time, your skills, or something you made.

steps.title: Two people vouch for you.
steps.body: Both of them already wear the pin. They help you get there, and then they say so.

steps.title: It goes on the record.
steps.body: Your Lab checks it and writes one line about what you did, next to your name.

steps.title: Pinned.
steps.body: At the next big get-together in your region, in front of everyone. The two people who vouched for you pin it on and say a few words.

given.note: There's no clock on any of this. Take the time it takes, and every kind of help counts.

status.title: The pin is forever. The seat takes showing up.
status.lede: Nobody takes the pin back. But the say that comes with it belongs to whoever's doing the work right now. Keep doing it, and it's yours.

items.label: Active
items.title: In the thick of it.
items.body: A seat in your Lab. A say in your region's playbooks, tools, kits and platform. Both are yours as long as you keep showing up.

items.label: Emeritus
items.title: Taking a step back.
items.body: Life happens. Step back and you keep the pin, the level, and your voice. When you're ready, take the next open seat.

decides.title: A few things that won't change.
rules: The pin is trust, not a trophy. The Labs hands you more of itself: the playbooks, the tools, the kits, the platform. Your region first. Take care of it.
No one can buy a pin, a level, or a vote.
Levels don't come with a vote, either. The boards look after programs, money, people and the brand.
The only way to lose a level is to seriously break the Code of Conduct.

join.title: Every pin starts with one small thing you did.
join.lede: The simplest way to start is the ambassador program. Share your story, bring someone to their first workshop, and see what you end up building.

footer.renders: Images of the pin are 3D renders, not photos. The real pins are still being made.
